# @workerstack/infra

Cloudflare infrastructure as code for workerstack repos

## Contents

- [@workerstack/infra](#workerstackinfra-1)
- [Config](#config)
- [Credentials](#credentials)

## @workerstack/infra

```sh
bun add -d @workerstack/infra
```

## Config

An `infra.config.ts` describes one product's infrastructure. It default-exports the result of `defineInfraConfig`, which checks the input and fills in defaults.

```ts
import { defineInfraConfig } from "@workerstack/infra";
import { defineEnv } from "@workerstack/repo/env";

// Normally its own file (`web.env.ts`) that the config imports; the account credentials live in its `global` block.
const env = defineEnv({
  dev: {},
  global: { CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210" },
  local: {},
  prod: {},
});

export default defineInfraConfig({
  env,
  cloudflare: {
    zone: { domain: "example.com", zoneId: "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" },
  },
  local: {
    host: "example.localhost",
    vars: (origin) => ({ APP_URL: origin.href }),
  },
});
```

`env` is any object with a `global` view of string values, such as a `defineEnv` instance. `defineInfraConfig` keeps it as given and never reads a value; a command reads the credentials (`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) when it runs. A secret field in the config is a type error.

### Products

A product is one `infra.config.ts`. Its name is its directory relative to the repo root, or `.` at the root.

`discoverProducts` finds every config under a root. `selectProducts` picks from them by target.

```ts
import { discoverProducts, selectProducts } from "@workerstack/infra";

const root = process.cwd();
const products = await discoverProducts(root);

selectProducts(root, products, undefined); // the only product, else an error
selectProducts(root, products, { all: true }); // every product
selectProducts(root, products, { name: "apps/web" }); // one product by name
```

The result is `{ ok: true, products }` or `{ ok: false, error }`.

## Credentials

Account credentials live in the product's env file, not in `infra.config.ts`. The config passes the env object. A command reads the credentials only when it runs.

```ts
// apps/web/web.env.ts
import { defineEnv, sealed } from "@workerstack/repo/env";

export const env = defineEnv({
  dev: {},
  global: {
    CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
    CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL: "ops@example.com",
    CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY: sealed("…"),
    CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: sealed("…"),
  },
  local: {},
  prod: {},
});
```

```ts
// apps/web/infra.config.ts
import { defineInfraConfig } from "@workerstack/infra";
import { defineEnv } from "@workerstack/repo/env";

// Normally imported from `./web.env.ts`.
const env = defineEnv({ dev: {}, global: { CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210" }, local: {}, prod: {} });

export default defineInfraConfig({
  env,
  cloudflare: { zone: { domain: "example.com", zoneId: "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" } },
});
```

Write a sealed value with `bun repo env set CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY --scope global`. The `env` field is typed `InfraEnv`: any object with a `global` view of string values.

### Keys

| Key                        | Needed by                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`    | `infra run`, `infra cf`   |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` | `infra run`, `infra cf`   |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY`       | `infra run`, `infra cf`   |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`     | `infra cf`                |

An empty string counts as missing.

### Commands

`infra run <dir> <command> [args...]` finds the product that holds `<dir>`. It runs the command with the wrangler credentials of that product. A token from your shell never leaks in.

`infra cf [args...]` finds the product that holds the current directory. It runs `cf` with that product's credentials. It returns the exit code of the child.

`cf` is a peer package. Install it with `bun add -d cf`.

### Errors

A missing key prints one line:

```console
infra run: CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY has no global value; run bun repo env set CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY --scope global
```

### Test runners

Both commands refuse to run when `VITEST` is set or `NODE_ENV` is `test`. The guard runs before any value is read, so a test never decrypts a secret. A test uses a fake instead.
